mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 5.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months indicates a contraction in industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in HOUST and a fall in RSAFS over the same month signals a shift from speculative investment to real-usage demand, which historically precedes a stabilization phase and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 0% and RSAFS < 0% in the same month
regime_hint: transition from speculative to real demand
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decrease in CPIAUCSL over two months signals a successful disinflationary tightening, which supports risk asset stability and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > previous month AND CPIAUCSL < previous month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in PAYEMS above trend by more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > trend by >0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent quarterly decline in GDPC1 for three consecutive quarters signals a deepening economic contraction, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.
